key_insight: A tetrahedral edge-strain interaction-potential formulation can reproduce hyperelastic passive response and active contraction while preserving continuum energetic coupling.
engineering_relevance: It offers a faster alternative to finite-element nonlinear solves for simulating active soft tissues such as myocardium, with better suitability for large-scale dynamic problems.
method: Recasts hyperelastic constitutive laws into tetrahedral edge strains rather than independent springs.
Implements active strain via a time-dependent activated reference configuration.
Adds an incompressibility treatment designed to avoid volumetric locking while retaining a continuum interpretation.
evidence_signal: The method is validated on multiple hyperelastic laws and a realistic ventricle case, showing preserved energy balance and literature-consistent longitudinal shortening and wall thickening.
watch_item: Accuracy and robustness will depend on how well the edge-based incompressibility and active-strain updates are implemented for highly nonlinear or near-incompressible regimes.
paper_title: An interaction potential method for passive and active dynamics of hyperelastic materials
